authored_reads.text: Denver's secondary loses its anchor and its eraser in the same report: Surtain II (shutdown corner, ankle) and Hufanga (safety, ankle) are both OUT, with Moss (ribs) questionable behind them. Without Surtain, Denver cannot travel its best corner with the opponent's WR1 or play the same rate of single-high man coverage; the structure bends toward zone and earlier safety help over the top. Without Hufanga, the robber / middle-hook eraser disappears, so middle-of-field crossers and seams have to be carried by linebackers and depth safeties. If Moss also sits, Denver is down its CB1 and CB3 by designation (Bryant is on IR), leaving a backup boundary corner across from the league's highest-volume receiving role and changing what the blitz can ask the back end to hold. That is an identity change, not a depth note: man rate, blitz willingness, and red-zone matchups all move with it. Bryant (IR) and Coleman (IR) remove the remaining corner/edge depth behind those absences. Seattle's losses are real but shallower: Charbonnet (knee/ACL) compresses the backfield to one primary back (power/goal-line and pass-pro snaps redistribute), and the Surratt/Thomas outs plus Neal and Price on IR thin special teams and defensive depth without changing either starting unit's identity. The asymmetry is the story of the week: one defense loses the players its scheme is built around; the other offense loses a committee piece.
